findings.finding: Seasonality on the company's own numbers puts Q1 revenue about $53.3-53.8M against a $52.05M bar (+2 to +3%). The bar, less RSR of ~$25.8M (the July-based $103M run rate / 4, +10% y/y on Q1 FY26's $23.4M), implies equipment of ~$26.3M, only +2% on Q1 FY26's $25.7M. Q4 FY26 equipment was $30.5M (+7.7%), with intrusion +36% and StarLink radio sales +40% y/y and +30% sequentially. Last year's Q4-to-Q1 equipment step (28.3 to 25.7, x0.91) applied to $30.5M gives ~$27.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been reliably bought. Q1 FY26 (2025-11-03) beat revenue by ~5% ($49.2M vs $46.8M) and EPS by $0.04, and the stock went -7.7%. Q2 FY26 (2026-02-02) was a small revenue beat with lock strength: +11.2%. Q3 FY26 (2026-05-04) was revenue in line with an EPS beat plus a litigation charge: -15.2%. Q4 FY26 (2026-08-24) beat $55.8M vs $52.5M: -1.3%. Equipment misses have been punished hardest (2025-02-03, distributor destocking: -26.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $52.05M is +5.9% y/y, below the +10-12% growth of every FY26 quarter, and implies equipment barely growing after a Q4 where radio sales grew 40%. If the market had priced the Q4 equipment exit rate, the bar would sit near $53.5M and the stock would not be 17% off its high with all six analysts at Buy. Caveat: this is my own seasonal arithmetic, not a company number, and Q1 FY26 equipment carried a door-locking surge that makes the comp harder.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 comparison numbers come from a different primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/69633/000110465925105432/nssc-20251030xex99d1.htm). StarLink +40% / +30% sequential is from https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/napcos-nssc-record-quarter-comes-with-a-costly-asterisk-attached-1825271/. Allegion's peer read is filed separately as its own finding.

findings.finding: RSR should print about $25.7-26.0M (+10-11% y/y), inside what the company already signalled with a ~$103M July-based run rate. On the Q4 call the CEO said the radio-sales benefit to RSR becomes more visible in the back half of FY27, so no Q1 acceleration is guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RSR has grown 11-13% steadily and has not been the swing line. The big moves came on equipment and one-offs.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the company's own guided run rate. The small positive is a possible upside surprise if August-September radio activations lifted the run rate above $103M. The market would see that in the new run-rate number disclosed with the release.
findings.independence: The back-half-FY27 timing comes from Q4 call coverage summarised in search results (https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/08/61400577/napco-security-techs-q4-2026-earnings-call-complete-transcript, 403 on fetch, snippet only). Shares the Q4 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: Allegion, the largest US commercial door-hardware peer, reported on 2026-10-22, after Napco last spoke. For Q3 2026 (same Jul-Sep quarter) it showed Americas revenue +11.7% (+9.1% organic), Americas non-residential up low double digits organically on volume and price, and a raised full-year organic guide to 5-6%. This points to firm demand in the school, healthcare and institutional door-locking channel that Napco's Marks/Alarm Lock products sell into.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Door-locking strength drove Napco's equipment growth in FY26 and the +11.2% reaction on 2026-02-02 ('electronic locks boost 2Q sales').
findings.why_not_priced: Napco's consensus has not moved off ~$52M since August despite a peer printing accelerating US non-residential hardware. A priced read-through would show estimate revisions and a stock closer to its high. This is a proxy: Napco has not confirmed the transmission, and its own access-control line fell 13.8% in Q4.
findings.independence: Independent company and document. Napco's own Q4 door-locking strength points the same way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000069633/000110465926100077/nssc-20260820xex99d1.htm).

findings.finding: In the FY26 10-K the company says it 'has submitted additional [IEEPA] claims which the Company cannot ensure the probability of collection and therefore, no refund receivable has been recognized related to these claims'. Any of those approved by CBP during Jul-Sep 2026 would land as another gross-margin benefit in Q1 FY27, like the ~600bp / $0.09 EPS benefit in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY26 beat carried ~$0.09 of tariff refunds and the stock went -1.3% on the day, then slid to ~$34.5 on insider sales. Refund-lifted EPS was not rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.37-0.38 matches the ex-refund run rate (Q4 $0.41 ex-refund in the Benzinga/MarketBeat comparison), so any further refund is outside the bar. As a one-off below the run-rate with no path to guidance, it is worth a fraction of its EPS. Status of CBP refund processing for Jul-Sep is unconfirmed; the latest public tally found was May 2026 (https://www.cato.org/blog/ieepa-refunds-update-good-progress-still-ways-go).

findings.finding: On the Q4 call the CFO flagged rising electronic-parts costs tied to data-center demand. Q4 equipment gross margin excluding the refund was roughly 26-27% (37.4% reported less ~11pp of refund on a $30.5M equipment base), about flat with Q1 FY26's 26.0%. Price increases are therefore no longer visibly lifting equipment margin, and Q1 equipment margin could compress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has been a swing line: the 2024-11 equipment-margin and sales miss went -14.4% (https://itiger.com/news/2480307668). Equipment margin expansion from price increases supported FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.37-0.38 on $52M implies operating margins similar to Q1 FY26's. A priced parts squeeze would show in EPS estimates cut below the prior-year rate of growth, which they are not. The CFO comment was qualitative, so the size is small.
findings.independence: The ex-refund margin arithmetic is from the Q4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000069633/000110465926100077/nssc-20260820xex99d1.htm) and Pulse 2.0's 55.3% ex-refund total GM (https://pulse2.com/napco-q4-gross-margin-jumps-850-basis-points-but-tariff-refunds-account-for-600-basis-points/).

findings.finding: Access control (Continental/MVP) sales fell 13.8% y/y in Q4 FY26 and 11% for FY26, and the CEO said MVP was not yet a meaningful contributor to recurring revenue. That drag continues into Q1 against the locking and intrusion strength.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction on this line. It was part of a Q4 that went -1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it was disclosed with Q4. The residual is that the low equipment bar in finding 1 may already reflect it, which is why finding 1 is held at +1.0.
findings.independence: Shares the Insider Monkey article with finding 5 (a different fact).

findings.finding: Founder and Executive Chairman Richard Soloway sold 475,000 shares on 2026-08-26/27 at $34.50-35.93 (about 43% of his direct holding; the Form 4 does not mark it as a 10b5-1 plan). Director Donna Soloway sold all 48,962 of her shares the same days. Both sales came two-thirds of the way through the quarter now being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sale coincided with the post-Q4 slide to ~$34.5 (the 52-week low area). The stock has since recovered to $39.08.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and was absorbed in late August, so the residual is only the information content of an insider selling heavily mid-quarter while seeing July-August trends. A more likely reading is estate or role-change diversification after he stepped up to executive chairman on 2026-07-08. If the market read it as a demand warning, estimates would have been cut, and they were not.
findings.independence: Donna Soloway's Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/69633/000141664626000002/primary_doc.xml). The new CEO's and the chairman's 2026-09-29 Form 4s are routine option grants at $37.90, not purchases.

findings.finding: Short interest of 2.48M shares at 8.7 days to cover (2026-10-15, ~6.9% of shares outstanding) on a name with ~293k average daily volume means a beat meets a short base that takes more than a week of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated. Feb 2026's +11.2% on a modest beat is consistent with short covering.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism, not a fact the price absorbs. The short base rose from 2.35M (2026-09-30) into the print, so it is not being covered ahead of it.
findings.independence: Insider Monkey cited 8.04% of float short on 2026-08-31 (https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/napcos-nssc-record-quarter-comes-with-a-costly-asterisk-attached-1825271/).
